records.name: Community Schools @Franklin S. Edmonds School
records.summary: A Community School partnership between the City, the School District and neighbors, Franklin S. Edmonds School welcomes volunteers through the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help with the school's programs for students and families, such as weekly grocery handouts for families and help at special events. The school also runs family forums, adult education classes, parent cafes, and after school and summer programs for young people.

first_step.how: Sign up through the city's volunteer portal, or ask the school's community school coordinator, Oanye Sims (oanye.sims@phila.gov, (215) 400-3370), about open shifts.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must clear background and child abuse checks before they work at the school, and the city page does not say what a first shift looks like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Before any shift, volunteers sign the district's code of conduct, get a district volunteer certificate, and complete clearance checks: the state child abuse history check, the state criminal background check, a city release waiver, and either an FBI waiver or fingerprinting. Open roles have included weekly help with grocery handouts for families and occasional help at special events.
first_visit_tips: Start the clearance paperwork early, because it has to be finished before your first shift.
Ask the coordinator which day and time the grocery handouts run.
Ask the coordinator where to check in on your first day.

records.notes: The city volunteer portal returned 403 in this run, so its clearance list, its open roles, its status and the 2026-10 activity date are carried over from tier 1 and were not re-read. The city school page says there are no upcoming events; the newest dated items on it are news posts from 2023 and the no-events note has no date, so confirm open shifts before treating this as active. A search result linked Philly Reading Coaches to this school, but the city page does not mention it, so it is not in the record. Tier 1 phone (215) 834-6277 is kept; the school's own listed number is (215) 400-3370.

records.name: Creating Opportunities for All
records.summary: A career training nonprofit for people with limited access to jobs. Participants take a 24 week set of skills modules in construction-related skills, computer literacy, project management and entrepreneurship, then can join optional team projects.
records.what_you_do: Take the 24 week skills program, which covers construction, architecture, engineering software, computer literacy, project management and entrepreneurship, then join optional team projects. The site does not list start dates, class times or fees, so ask on the contact form.

cost.text: No program fees are listed on the site. Free training and scholarships are mentioned only for the youth division.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form at cofa-cov.org to ask how to apply for the next 24 week training and when it starts. The site does not describe an application.
first_step.basis: The program is aimed at people with limited access to jobs, but the site does not say how to apply, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The program is 24 weeks of skills modules, and team projects are optional after that. The site does not say how long each session runs or what the course costs.
first_visit_tips: Ask on the contact form for the start date, class times and cost before you plan around them.
Ask whether the course needs a laptop or other equipment, since the site does not say.

records.notes: One website page with a contact form only: no program pages, dates, fees, training address, phone or email. The site's contact page returned 404 in this run. The tier 1 contact name 'Creating Opportunities for Vetera' is a cut-off organization name, not a person, so it was removed. This record and creating-opportunities-for-youth-empowerment-inc share one website, and the site describes the youth division as a division of this group, so the owner may want to decide whether the two should be one record. The site also runs a veterans track (COV) that has no record of its own. Copyright 2026 and older team bio dates are not activity evidence.

records.name: Creating Opportunities for Youth Empowerment (COFYE)
records.summary: The youth division of Creating Opportunities for All, for middle and high school students ages 12 to 20. Students learn construction, architecture and engineering software skills and work on hands-on projects such as affordable housing and tiny homes.
records.what_you_do: Take the youth program's skills training in construction, project management, architecture, engineering software and entrepreneurship, then work on hands-on projects. The program links to school STEM and career technical classes. The site does not give class times or start dates.

cost.text: The youth division mentions scholarships and free training, with no details on who qualifies. No prices are listed.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on cofa-cov.org to ask about the next youth start date or about scholarships.
first_step.basis: The youth program is a set course, and the site gives no start dates or enrollment steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Students learn construction, architecture and engineering software skills, then join hands-on projects such as affordable housing and tiny homes. The program works with schools and links to school STEM and career technical classes. The site does not say how long a session runs or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Ask about scholarships before you commit, since the site mentions them without details.
Ask which school or site hosts the class, since the program works through school partnerships.

records.notes: Shares its website with creating-opportunities-for-all-inc. The site gives 24 weeks for the adult program only, so the 24 week length from tier 1 was removed here. The veterans track (COV) is not a youth program, so veterans were removed from this record's audience; the veterans track has no record of its own yet. The name was corrected from 'Creating Opportunities for All' to the youth division name the site uses (COFYE); the full name matches the IRS alternate name. Contact name kept from tier 1 (not confirmed on the site).

records.name: Curricula for the Community
records.summary: A literacy nonprofit that tutors children ages 3 to 10 one on one and coaches families on reading at home. It also works with schools.
records.what_you_do: Families book one on one tutoring with a learning plan made for each child, or join family literacy sessions one on one or in groups. Schools can book teacher training and small group sessions for students.

cost.text: The site lists no prices or fees, and does not say whether tutoring is free or paid.

first_step.how: Book a consultation on the Appointments page, or send the contact form, and ask about one on one tutoring for a child ages 3 to 10.
first_step.basis: Families start with a booked consultation, and the site lists no prices, class times or session locations.
first_step.what_to_expect: The first step is a booked consultation, where the team offers tailored guidance on educational goals. Tutoring for ages 3 to 10 is one on one and starts from a learning plan made for the child. The site does not give the length of a consultation, the cost, or where sessions are held.
first_visit_tips: Have your child's age and reading goals in mind before you book.
Ask whether sessions are in person or online, since the site does not say.
Ask about fees before you book, since none are listed.

records.notes: The site has no dated events or news, so status is probably_active on the basis of a working site. The About page gives no street address for services, no hours, no phone number and no statement on whether services are in person or online. The contact form is also for groups that want to work together. The site has a cart and a donations page; neither was opened. Contact name kept from tier 1 (not shown on the site).

records.name: Fostering Success Boys to Men
records.summary: A nonprofit that coaches and mentors at-risk boys and young men through workshops, a youth leadership academy, and street outreach. It also runs transitional housing.
records.what_you_do: Young people and their caregivers can ask about the youth leadership academy, the rites of passage program, the STEM leaders program, and the workshops. Other named programs include a career skills workshop, a talk series on community issues, and street outreach and group home services for young people who are runaway, homeless or on the street.

cost.text: The site has a donation button. Program costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Send a message through the contact form on the homepage, or call (267) 650-9616, and ask which youth program is taking people now and who can join.
first_step.basis: The site describes its programs but does not explain how a young person enrolls or who is eligible.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical session, meeting place or schedule. Programs include a leadership academy, a STEM program and workshops, and the group also runs street outreach. Calling or messaging the group is the only way we found to learn times, places and eligibility.
first_visit_tips: Ask about times and the meeting place before you come, since the site lists neither.
Ask whether any program has a cost, since none is listed.

records.notes: Single-page site. Its navigation links all return to the homepage, so there are no program, events or volunteer pages to read. Copyright 2024 and the 2016 founding year are not activity evidence. Eligibility, age ranges, costs and schedules are not published. The tier 1 'Chat with us' label was changed to the homepage contact form, which is what the page shows. The two tier 1 location entries were the same address and were merged.

records.name: Hands Elevated for a Purpose
records.summary: Neighbors who share personal care products with students in underserved parts of Philadelphia, keep a list of free places for food and basic supplies, and give children chances to explore beyond their neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the group's volunteer form to help with the personal care and youth programs, and check the events page for job fairs and other dated events. To ask about personal care products or help, use the contact page; the site does not say how those requests are handled.

schedule.text: The site lists no weekly schedule. Events, such as job fairs, are posted on the events page as they come up.

locations.label: Mailing address (IRS)
locations.address: 1116 E Mount Airy Ave Apt C24, Philadelphia, PA 19150

cost.text: Donations go through PayPal. The site does not say whether any program has a fee.

first_step.how: Ask through the contact page what volunteers do and how to sign up, then fill in the volunteer form linked from the site menu.
first_step.basis: The volunteer form returned a sign-in error when we read it, and the site does not say what volunteering involves, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say what volunteers do, how long a shift runs, or how often help is needed. The group works on personal care products and youth programs, so ask on the contact page what the current need is before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: If the volunteer form asks you to sign in, ask the group for another way to sign up.
Check the events page for job fairs and other dated events before you plan a visit.

records.notes: The group's full name on its site is Hands Elevated for a Purpose (H.E.L.P Inc.). The events page shows its dated events only in link addresses and flyer file names, for example a May 16, 2026 spring job fair; the page text has no dates, so the 2026-05 evidence rests on that link. The site says the personal care project was planned to launch in spring 2025 and does not say whether it runs now. The volunteer form (forms.gle link) returned 401 Unauthorized, so its questions were not seen and nothing was submitted. The contact page address (1500 Chestnut Street, Suite 2 #2344) has a suite number that looks like a mailbox; check before showing it as a place to visit.

records.name: Holy Family Formation and Education Center
records.summary: A faith formation center that runs religion classes for children from toddlers to teens, supports parents who raise their children in the faith, and trains catechists, the religion teachers.
records.what_you_do: Parents enroll children in the formation programs, which are grounded in scripture and the liturgy, and new teachers can train as catechists. The site does not explain how to sign up.

cost.text: The site lists no prices or tuition.

first_step.how: Contact the center through holyfamilycgs.org to ask about enrolling a child or training as a catechist. The site lists no phone number, email or sign-up steps, so the website is the only contact we found.
first_step.basis: The site gives no sign-up steps or contact details, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical class, how long classes run, or what a first visit looks like. Its programs are based on scripture and the liturgy and run for children from toddlers through teens. The center reports 120 children enrolled in 2025, so classes do have students.
first_visit_tips: Ask how to enroll before you plan a visit, since the site has no sign-up steps.
Ask about class times and cost, which the site does not list.

records.notes: One-page site. Its only links are to the homepage and to a grant funder, Do Good Foundation, which is named under recent grants and was not opened. No denomination is named. The wording (catechists, liturgy, Catechesis of the Good Shepherd) suggests a Catholic setting, but the site does not say so, so the faith field is left unset. Copyright 2026 is not used as evidence; the July 2025 catechist training and the 2025 enrollment figure are the newest dated facts. The 'Do Good Foundation' grant source was not added to leads because a grant funder is likely a private foundation, which is out of scope.
